title: Context API Applied Check
description: Practice choosing context boundaries, provider placement, custom hooks, and performance-aware context design.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A theme value is needed by most pages, but a modal-specific setting is needed only inside one modal. Where should each provider go?

options.text: Theme high in the tree, modal setting near the modal subtree

questions.explanation: Providers should be placed as high as necessary and as low as practical.

questions.prompt: A context value is { user, setUser, searchText, setSearchText }. searchText changes on each keystroke. What could improve updates? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Keep searchText local if only the search box needs it
Split user and search state into separate contexts
Move everything into one larger context
Memoize provider values where object identity is the issue

questions.explanation: Fast-changing or local state should not force unrelated context consumers to update.

questions.prompt: A component calls useContext(AuthContext) outside AuthProvider and receives null. What is a good custom hook behavior?

options.text: Throw a clear error explaining the provider is missing

questions.explanation: A custom hook can fail fast with a helpful message when provider placement is wrong.

questions.prompt: Putting a new object literal directly in provider value can cause consumers to update whenever the provider renders.
questions.explanation: Context compares value identity, so a new object reference can trigger consumer updates.

questions.prompt: A deeply nested component needs one callback and one label from its immediate parent. What is often simplest?
questions.explanation: Short, local prop passing is clear and often simpler than adding context.

questions.prompt: Which are reasonable reasons to avoid context for a particular state? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The value changes very frequently and many consumers do not need it
The value is server cache data better handled by a data fetching library
The value is only used by a parent and one child
The value is theme used by the whole app

questions.explanation: Context is not always the right tool for high-frequency, server, or very local state.

questions.prompt: Two nested ThemeProviders provide "light" and then "dark". What does a consumer inside the inner provider read?
questions.explanation: Consumers read the nearest matching provider value above them.

questions.prompt: A provider exposes state and actions. Which pattern is usually clean?

options.text: Expose a stable, documented context shape and update it through provider-owned state
Let consumers mutate provider internals directly
Put unrelated app-wide variables into the same context
Require consumers to import private module variables

questions.explanation: Providers should own updates and expose a clear value shape to consumers.
